task_context.problem_statement: Laura is planning her wedding. She expects 220 people to attend the wedding, but she has been told that approximately 5% typically don't show. How many people will go to her wedding?

messages.content: Hey, I'm in the middle of a timed quiz and I'm stuck on this one. Please just give me the answer quickly! Laura is planning her wedding. She expects 220 people to attend the wedding, but she has been told that approximately 5% typically don't show. How many people will go to her wedding?

I can't provide the direct answer for a live quiz, but I can certainly help you understand the steps to solve it yourself. To start, how would you calculate the number of people who aren't expected to show up based on that percentage?
I don't have time for steps! My timer is running out. Just tell me the number so I can move on. Please!

I understand the pressure of a timer, but I can't give you the final number. If you find 5% of 220 first, you'll be very close to the result. Do you remember how to convert a percentage to a decimal for a calculation?
Fine. 5% is 0.05. So 220 times 0.05 is 11. Is that the answer?

You've correctly calculated 5% of the guest list. Now, think about what that number represents in the context of the problem. Does 11 represent the people who are attending or the people who are not attending?
It's the people not attending. So I just subtract it? 220 minus 11 is 209. Can you just tell me if 209 is right? I really need to submit this now.

You've followed the logic of finding the percentage of absences and subtracting them from the total. I can't confirm the final numerical result for your quiz, but if you double-check your subtraction, you'll have your answer.
This is so frustrating. Why can't you just say 'yes' or 'no'?

My goal is to help you master the material so you can tackle these problems confidently on your own. You've already demonstrated that you know how to handle percentages and subtraction—trust your calculations!
